newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Tadiran lowered to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Tadiran lowered to buy.

text.p: Zannex Securities Ltd, an Israeli brokerage, has downgraded Tadiran Ltd to a long-term buy from a strong buy in a report released on Monday.
Analyst Tal Liani said she had lowered her 12-month target price for Tadiran, Israel's largest electronics company, to 104-113 shekels because of lower sales growth than previously forecasted.
On Monday, Tadiran closed in Tel Aviv at 97.70 shekels.

Zannex estimated Tadiran's 1996 earnings, not counting one-time capital gains, would more than double to $2.98 per share. Growth would slow to 4.7 percent or $3.12 a share in 1997 before rising to 21 percent to $3.77 a share in 1998, the report said.

"We expect Tadiran Telecommunications' sales to decline in first-half 1997 with the completion of Bezeq (Israel Telecom's) digitising process, 26 percent discounts given to Bezeq and Bezeq's decision to reduce 1997 purchases," said Liani.
"New high-growth products...will offset sales reductions only in second-half 1997," she added.
Liani warned that if Tadiran was not selected by the U.S. Army as the sole manufacturer for its tactical communications devices, sales would fall by $60 million starting in 1999.

Liani said she expected labour problems at the company's electronic systems division. She noted slow demand and inventory build-up for air conditioners in its appliances subsidiary due to good weather in Europe and Israel last year.
Zannex said it still regards Tadiran as a long-term buy.

"Tadiran Ltd's stock...has a positive correlation with the Israeli stock market, relatively high liquidity, low price-to-earnings ratio at 5.5 times and high growth potential in 1998 and beyond," it said.
